summary: Fixed-block message pool with a small send/dispatch layer over a caller-provided byte array. In v1 msg_encode releases the buffer when it fails, and msg_send releases it a second time, so the block sits on the free list twice and later allocations alias each other (double free, CWE-415); v2 drops the second release and also makes mp_release ignore blocks that are not in use; v3 is a behaviour-preserving refactor of v2.

pairs.intent: CWE-415 fix: msg_send no longer releases the buffer after msg_encode failed (msg_encode already did), mp_release becomes idempotent for free blocks via the new mp_is_used helper, and the now-dead legacy wrapper msg_free is removed. msg_reply, which never double-released, is untouched.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: CWE-415: on msg_encode failure the block was released by msg_encode and again through msg_free, leaving a cycle in the free list; v2 returns the error without a second release.

truth.label: changed
truth.notes: defence in depth: a block whose header is not MP_STATE_USED is ignored, so a repeated release can no longer corrupt the free list or underflow in_use.

truth.label: removed
truth.notes: legacy wrapper around mp_release whose only caller was the buggy path

pairs.intent: Behaviour-preserving refactor of v2: operand and store order, loop style, renames, simplified boolean return, and the field accessors moved above msg_encode.
